account:
Today I kept morning office and came to the mill for my ten o'clock grain inspection. It is now 11:02, but nobody has shown me the grain stocks or identified their manager. The secretary is beside me with the appointment book; I have asked who arranged the inspection and who is responsible for the mill. Lunch at home is scheduled for noon.

The unusual thing is the repeated phrase 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Several townsfolk have said essentially the same words, but none has supplied concrete details that I have heard. The builder has heard the rumour too, but reports no confirmed damage and does not know who manages the grain. Yesterday he likewise reported no confirmed defects at the bridge, landing, or warehouse approach. I have authorized neither repairs nor spending.

The baker offered bread for meetings this morning, though I placed no order. He said he knew of no gatherings; the innkeeper reportedly had no guests or bread orders. A townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread, which could simply be ordinary bakery business. I have no evidence connecting that sack to any secret meeting.

I suspect there may be some proposed change involving the bakery and river crossings or transport, or merely a rumour being repeated around town. I do not yet know its purpose or origin. The builder is investigating the same vague talk, not presenting a definite project. I need a direct explanation from the baker or an identifiable firsthand witness rather than treating repetition as confirmation. For now the secretary can help clarify the inspection arrangements and keep an accurate record of what is—and is not—known.
